name: JŪ MǍ PĀO 車馬包
description: Jū mǎ pāo (Chariot Horse Cannon) is a traditional Chinese matching and trick-taking game that uniquely utilizes the 32 pieces of a Chinese Chess (Xiangqi) set as cards. Played by 3 or 4 players, players treat the chess discs as a deck, shuffling them face-down and forming stacks. It is a game of memory, piece-value calculation, and specific combination-based captures.

content.text: Jū mǎ pāo (Chariot Horse Cannon) is a traditional Chinese matching and trick-taking game that uniquely utilizes the 32 pieces of a Chinese Chess (Xiangqi) set as cards. Played by 3 or 4 players, players treat the chess discs as a deck, shuffling them face-down and forming stacks. It is a game of memory, piece-value calculation, and specific combination-based captures.
Dates back to the late Qing dynasty or earlier. The use of Xiangqi pieces as cards is a common practice in Southern China and Southeast Asia (see 'Giog' in Malaysia).

Three or four players. The game is best with three, in which case each receives eight pieces; with four players the 32 Xiangqi pieces are distributed evenly (typically eight per player). No partnerships; each plays for themselves.
A full set of 32 Chinese Chess pieces (16 Red, 16 Black).
A full set of 32 Chinese Chess pieces (16 Red, 16 Black).
Pieces are shuffled face-down and arranged in 16 stacks of two in a circle. Each player draws a set number of pieces (usually 8).
